en: A spirit of the dream world. All who sleep are said to appear in Lukoje's world. On leaving it, that is, on waking, Lukoje erases their memories. But Lukoje sleeps too, and only then, they say, can one bring back memories and things from the dream.

A Demon Duke able to physically absorb and dominate others. That power made Animacie overwhelming, but it all went wrong after teaming with Dromea to snare a certain demon and eating its arm. Its body, once obedient, went haywire and began to warp wildly.
note: editorial: 'once easily controlled, began warping out of control' repeated 'control'; reworded, same meaning.

en: A Demon Duke, head of Espel-Dex. He sends his demons to many lands for useful results, aiming at last to "negotiate with the gods." Strong, yet he prefers economic and political battles. Revering his ancestor Pel-Dex, he calls himself the second Pel-Dex.

A Demon Duke known as the Grand Chancellor. With Tsakaro's power, he gathers all kinds of information and trades it with other Demon Dukes: Hilde, Zoze, Ixgoil, Espel-Dex and more. Seen as a danger even by the gods, he rarely stays in one place.

A Demon Duke called the Lady of Darkness. She can't bear anyone lovelier or more glamorous than herself, and uses any dirty trick to bring them down. A master schemer, she's strong in battle too: her lower half attacks, her upper half casts. No openings.

A Demon Duke who rules all cats, and could found a cat kingdom at will. Once just a demon cat, kept by a certain Demon Duke. But she fell into a vile trap, lost both arms and was banished. To avenge her, the cat rose up with the keepsake she left behind.

A great demon-spirit monument haunting the lands, binding many souls within. The Path of Souls of the god of Dark Oblivion is flawed: at times souls of the in-between arise as cursed wills. Apasha gathers them. It can steal souls; even Demon Dukes shun it.
note: accuracy: restored the dropped risk ([JP]) as the reason Demon Dukes avoid it; [JP] = haunting.

en: A dragon worshiped by both the forsaken folk and the Kin of Darkness of a small Wasteland. Life was simple but calm, till one night it and both their leaders fell into a strange stupor and erased the land. They say it still suffers, regretting that night.
note: accuracy: restored [JP] (still suffers) and the hearsay [JP].

en: A Demon Duke feared as a War General, as is Velkirios. Likes the strong, but likes even more the weak who still fight back with all they have. Dantarius fought Velkirios many times, and at the cost of a leg cut Velkirios's arms down to their present count.
note: editorial: moved 'even more' next to the verb (it trailed the long object).

en: Demon Duke Zoze's daughter. Since Mirco tied a ribbon on her precious Harz Crystal, she's loved him and dreams of slaying him herself someday. Honest, but very slow. With Zoze's might, no one can stop her antics: a menace. No one's seen under her skirt.
note: accuracy: restored [JP] (a menace) to the antics sentence.

en: Homunculus siblings, elder sister Alba and younger brother Berta. Their maker, a famed alchemist, for some reason tried to dispose of them. Now self-aware, they resisted and killed their maker, but their bodies began to crumble. They roam, seeking a home.

A Demon Duke. What he's thinking with those round little eyes is a mystery, but he seems to want to pass on his factors. His wobbly body just begs to be poked. When he goes for a walk, Ira comes to play by nuking his wobbly belly. 'Oh, Nyooop!?'

A Demon Duke. Once, in a Wasteland, nuke after nuke made an Ultimate Mana Source. The magic seemed set to scatter, but suddenly shrank, birthing a huge True Crystal and a demon girl. Childish yet cruel, her peerless magic destroys till all life kneels.

A Demon Duke. Head of the noble House Lenzer, revered by the dark knights. He wields the demon axe Baltagias, said to kill any weakling who touches it. Even the Wastelands have laws to keep: to stop Zoze's lawlessness, Dalisiamarte joins hands with Hilde.

Not for loan:
207591.584
Addendum 'Fell Wound'
Kin of Darkness Pel-Dex visits Yanal, Nmachi sys.; meets King of Ada; both curse gods. Pel-Dex cuts Mixia, the watching god of existence: first god wounded. Names self Demon Duke. Gods' fleshly descent unwise.
note: accuracy: restored the source's repeated subject Pel-Dex for the cut (the English read as if both cut Mixia).

Not for loan:
------.---
'Hevayur'
Hevayur promoted from library staff to deputy librarian on Void's recommendation. That makes three deputies, but only Hevayur has a god's recommendation. Is the next librarian settled?

Not for loan:
605213.203
'A Void Axis Appears'
Void Axis seen in Kuus, Mashitra system. Took sibling form, roamed lands; as in past reports, lacking resistance, bodies crumbled. Deemed harmless, but Grand Chancellor neared it in a New Land. Watch.

Not for loan:
000023.006
'Apasha's Atonement Stone'
Apasha, first god of Dark Oblivion, laid the Path of Souls; a hidden flaw spread to all lands since the Primal Soil. Too late. Grief-mad, Apasha became a memorial for undying souls. Fix left to heirs.

Not for loan:
580034.115
Addendum 'Kin of Darkness Strife'
At Arion Dafa, Demon Duke Shantiba falls to Animacie and Dromea's scheme; power sapped, wanders. Her threat thus ends. But her demon cat licked the witch's blood, mutated by grudge: new threat.

Not for loan:
------.---
'Void Named Chief God'
Long-rumored Void becomes god of space. Void's scenario for creating the Eld: perfect, in a word. With Void as chief, the six gods take the first step to glory and victory. First: sorting out the lands.

Not for loan:
714729.301
'Bone Dragon's Deicide'
Bone Demon Dragon learns why its land fell; rages. Deicide bid past the Horizon rocks Wastes, Divine Realm; System oddly idle. Unforeseen war on the Horizon: hard to enter, no exit. Target: Ahadaram's head.
note: accuracy: restored the dropped [JP] (the war is on the Horizon, hard to enter, no exit).

en:
Not for loan:
------.---
'The One Called Grand Chancellor'
Conduct of the dark world's Grand Chancellor not to be ignored. Meets many Kin of Darkness, gains much lore; knowing too much is most displeasing. Their words stir the lands. Capture: grand escape.

Not for loan:
714729.301
'Urnas Rade'
This Zefkaka has a very bad attitude.

Cheerful and jolly, a Devilish woman who guzzles drinks while laughing with her customers. Jolly but careless, she misses the little details. That causes some blunders, but apparently a good night's sleep is enough for her to forget anything unpleasant.

A girl who makes her living from the inn her parents left her. It's the only link left to them, so she works as hard as she can to keep it. Maybe that's why she's strict about money, and spends her days let down by adventurers who sleep in the stables.

The sharp Director of Administration, a minister in effect. Costo's family has long advised the Bistel royals, and is respected beyond Bistel. But he has one grave flaw: as a noble, he has no idea what things cost. Hence his demotion to the item shop.

A priest at the Temple of Orses who heals the illnesses of adventurers and ordinary folk, and gives them advice. He shows understanding toward all things, and listens from the other person's point of view.

Orphaned by an epidemic as a child, she was taken in by Saines. On a trip to a nearby town, a spirit drifted up to Saines, who heard its grief at becoming a soul of the in-between and purified it. Moved, she took an interest in laying spirits to rest.

The young Queen of Bistel. For generations the Bistel royal family has held the highest authority as priests of Fiona, the Earth Goddess, and only she can hear Fiona's words directly, as oracles. Off duty, Ragnastia is rather easygoing.

A clerk who works at the Bistel Training Hall. Whenever she spots adventurers, she eagerly calls out to them. She walks the town so diligently that there's hardly anyone in Bistel who doesn't know her face.

A Dragonfolk Lord who raises heroes. Finding a crowd, Rondelgius takes the most visible spot, and any passing adventurer who seems "the one!" gets an impossible task. Special talent: weaving through crowds to a target without once looking away.

A bard who wanders from land to land. Breezy looks give a frivolous, flashy impression, but the bard's passion for song and dedication to studying it are the real thing. Special talent: playing any song after hearing it just once.
note: editorial: 'The breezy looks / the passion' read as unattached; tied to 'the bard' (gender not settled).

en: Head of House Barnefon, one of two surviving Great Houses of Isfald. All three are of royal blood and take the throne if the royal line dies out. The third plotted to kill the royals and was purged by the people. He's carefree, caring only for antiques.
note: editorial: one term for [JP] ('Great Houses'; the row also said 'Three Houses': now 'All three'); 'the line' -> 'the royal line'.

en: A scatterbrained, clumsy fairy who ran a small bazaar in the forest, then, wanting more, came all the way to Isfald. But trade that worked in the forest draws no notice in the city: a real problem. The stock is all unusual, so alchemists like the shop.

First Princess of Isfald. Elves grow worldly with politics and money after long in a city, but at heart Leafa stays pure, which makes her a bit of a nuisance to her father the king and his circle. Kept from politics, she wants people who'll do her bidding.

A Yotel Wharf auntie with an only son, Gregorio. She's forever worrying whether Gregorio is bothering people, whether he'll ever stand on his own two feet, and so on. The more trouble a child is, the dearer they are, as the saying goes.

An old man whose every catch gets snatched by Muse. He used to cheer aloud at every fish he landed, but now, wary of Muse, he tries to make himself unnoticeable. For all his efforts, though, Muse still swipes them.
Benef, his youthful strength restored. Now there's no fish he can't catch. Every fish will dance to the tune of his rod.

A wandering Werebeast girl who turned up in this port town a few years ago. When Benef, on a whim, fed the starving Muse a fish, she thought, "This geezer's useful, nya! Stick with him for all-you-can-eat fish, nya!" She's chased his fish ever since.

Muse is an avatar of the Edumo. A Senior is allowed some free action. Long ago it came to this land to eat it all, but agreed to wait when asked by Fiona and the King of Bistel of the day. When starving, Muse turns back into the Edumo and hunts the land.

Owner of a shady antique shop in Saimar. Highly resistant to cursed goods: your average ill-omened item won't make Bilente flinch. Walmitt and the other Saimar merchants have secretly put up a bounty: '1,000,000 GP to whoever can startle Bilente.'

The head of merchants is a Chief Merchant, and the head of the Chief Merchants is the Grand Merchant, a post they elect. Walmitt is already serving a third term, and knows it's time to raise a successor, but has no one to trust with it.
note: editorial: 'in a third term' unidiomatic; joined the two sentences to drop the repeated name (no pronoun: gender not in glossary).

en: A Gandra Mine alchemist who lives by smithing and alchemy. A Rubenburg graduate, same year as Vice Principal Kathleen, but skipped dull classes like Ancient Language and was held back twice or so. Once hit on Jera and came back white as a sheet, they say.

A man who's simply in the way. Why, of all places, does he hang around the floor that handles food? He's loathed in the Canteen, and it can't be helped. Nobody can stand someone retching right beside them during a nice break from work.

A little cook who works in the Canteen. Tris was made by Tarmeet and is packed with his obsessions about the ideal magic puppet, which makes Tris a bit inflexible at times. In spare moments, Tris loves baking sweets and taking them to Jeratan to play.

Supposedly the one woman at Gandra Mine. Jera ran the store normally at first, but after dressing up for an event, something awoke. Insiders smirk when a newcomer makes eyes at Jera. Jera truly seeks love, so smiles wryly each time the truth comes out.

Mascot of Jera's General Store. Tarmeet built it in Jera's likeness, and Jera remodeled it. At first it was meant to be just a doll, so it was hung from a pillar, and the habit seems to have stuck. It's adorable flailing its arms and legs while hanging.
The man who runs Gandra Mine. Stubborn, he chews people out without hearing them, but his thinking and his skills are sound, so he's well regarded.

An old fairy over 900 years of age. With the old liveliness long gone, Quasimon just sits plopped in the plaza. The fairy has become a famous sight of Harjiradam, but what does Quasimon think of that?
note: editorial: the name was repeated three times in three sentences; one replaced by 'the fairy' (gender not settled).

en: A shrine maiden who prays for the peace of the land, now 87. No regrets over a life of prayer, but always wonders, "What if I'd lived differently..." Loves the fan-tossing game; she told Namina, who at once proposed playing it with Quasimon. One more joy!
note: editorial: 'told of it, Namina had a flash' was a dangling clause; restated who told whom (source: she told Namina).

en: A girl who adores Archbishop Mersenne. In Namina's childhood, Mersenne came to the village with Semnadoc's teachings. Moved by them, Namina came here, but lately seems to have forgotten them a little. At such a sensitive age, maybe it can't be helped.
note: editorial: lead decision, no she/her for Namina; rephrased with the name.

en: A go-getter merchant of Semnadoc, always chasing what's new. She's eager to sell herself to other towns, but among merchants she's already well known as Semnadoc's go-getter girl. She wants to open a branch, and for a while Lunea's Shop was a candidate.

Semnadoc's young Archbishop, who as a child saw the giant goddess statue, fell for it, swore to become Archbishop, and did. Each morning at the temple door he looks up, cries "O great, fair Semnadoc, thanks for your mercy today too!!" 10 times, and weeps.

A spacey Gnome Priest with a drawn-out way of talking. Gives career guidance at Rubenburg. Bad kids get a "That's no goood~?" lecture until they turn good. Sometimes freezes mid-smile. It may startle you at first, but it's Professor Harmoni, so it's fine.

Gives career guidance in evil, with Professor Harmoni. Brilliant, sensible, reliable: the opposite of Professor Harmoni in every way, so some students whisper Warmoni is a doppelganger summoned by arcane arts. One tried an ambush interview. No word since.

A girl gifted for magic. Her rare talent took her out of the Training Hall to study at Rubenburg. Stubborn, a sore loser and a hard worker, she went on to graduate top of her class. Her dream is to use her power for the land and its people.
A Skunk Girl in a fix, kicked out of job after job because she gasses everywhere she goes. She came here thinking a church would surely give her work.

A gentle, meek rich boy, trying hard to act grown-up so he can lead the dark world. He leans on his wet nurse Gurtia for everything. Never doubting anyone, he's unlikely to learn her true feelings. He swings the "demon sword baltagias" his uncle gave him.

A bully. A true sadist. Her position has her obey Mirco, but she sees it as training the hopeless boy. If his life is truly at risk, she'll save him, grudgingly. Seeing him cry is her hobby and greatest joy. Mirco never sees he's bullied, and adores her.

A sincere, kind elder devoted to House Lenzer, doting on Mirco like a grandchild. Mirco's lack of strength and leadership is a worry, but Hess trusts he'll be a fine head one day. No match for the young women, Hess panics when they make Mirco cry.

Once fought Dalisiamarte alone and lost utterly. Conceding, Zephal tried to die by the blade on the spot, but Dalisiamarte liked that; over drinks they bonded, and Zephal swore his soul's obedience. Now a top Lenzer swordsman, he too despairs of Mirco.

A tomboyish harpy who lived near House Lenzer and often teased Mirco. One day Gurtia caught her at it, but far from scolding her, gave her a lecture on how to enjoy Mirco. Since then she's looked up to Gurtia as her master (in Mirco-teasing).

A custom griffon made for Mirco, but Zapper won't carry the green Mirco and pays him no mind. Mirco once jumped the sleeping Zapper to ride by force, was caught halfway and beaten to a pulp. It wasn't about the ride: Zapper was angry at the cowardly act.
note: editorial: first sentence had no clear subject for 'with no intention'; 'he was angry' was ambiguous (Mirco or Zapper).

en: A Raizam, worn out and frazzled deep beneath the desert. Somehow, the Blanc Desert seems to be an uncomfortable place for him. Is there something there he can't stand?
Monster Name
Item Name
!Roma

Alchemy Item No. 1.
Air Fruit. This lets you breathe even underwater. With it, you can even explore underwater dungeons.

>Frozen Elven Iron x Vectreim
>Vectreim x Tri-Layer Orat

Alchemy Item No. 2.
Angel's Window. When you enter a cave, it shows your surroundings in a little window. Make one if you don't want to get lost.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Frozen Elven Iron

Alchemy Item No. 3.
Rock Counter. It tells you how many stone blocks are on the floor. If a square on your map just won't fill in, it may be stone, so try it.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Tri-Layer Orat
>Vectreim x Mazurite

Alchemy Item No. 4.
Dove Bell. This drives off the enemies lying in wait on the floor. Try it when you want to breeze through.

>Frozen Elven Iron x Mazurite
>Mazurite x Tri-Layer Orat

Alchemy Item No. 5.
Crow Bell. Some monsters guard certain rooms. Once beaten, they stay gone until you change floors, but ring this and they return.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Vectreim
>Tri-Layer Orat x Milstone

Alchemy Item No. 6.
Sheep's Brush. It marks enemies lying in wait when you view the map. Just carrying it helps, so make at least one.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Mazurite
>Frozen Elven Iron x Milstone

Alchemy Item No. 7.
Bone Slippers. If your party is wiped out, these send you home automatically. As corpses, of course.

>Dvel Soft Steel x Milstone
>Frozen Elven Iron x Tri-Layer Orat

Alchemy Item No. 8.
Death Pinwheel. When enemies appear, it tells you their level. If the gap is too wide, knowing when to run matters too!

>Vectreim x Milstone

Alchemy Item No. 9.
Dice of Fate. Countless probabilities can come into play in any situation. If you could see them, would you be able to accept your own fate? Try these dice and find out.

>Mazurite x Milstone
note: accuracy: restored the source's > recipe mark (as in the other RENKIN rows). Proof: 'item' lowercase vs 'Item' elsewhere. | editorial: 'Alchemy Item' capitalised and the item name without 'The', as in rows 1-8.

en:
The ultimate alchemy item.
Philosopher's Stone.
Only those who have mastered alchemy can obtain it. They say it appears on its own once the conditions are met... but what might those conditions be?
note: editorial: item-name line without 'The', as in rows 1-9.
